result.title: TowerBridge: Bridging the Dual-Encoder Modality Gap via Weight-Space Programming
result.summary: CLIP-style dual encoders map images and text through two separate towers into a shared embedding space, where the two modalities occupy distinct regions separated by a modality gap. Retrieval fails when wrong matches, or hard negatives, outrank the correct one, and the gap is the usual suspect. Yet removing it post hoc degrades retrieval on every CLIP checkpoint we test. We introduce a paired statistic that identifies directions where the two towers agree more on hard negatives than on matched pairs. Mildly attenuating these directions improves retrieval while largely preserving the gap. We arrive at this correction through weight-space programming: guided by the statistic, an LLM agent inspects both towers and writes closed-form weight edits without backpropagation. Free to edit any component, the agent improves COCO test retrieval on all 13 CLIP checkpoints and edits an output projection in 12 of the 13. We distill and refine its recurring correction into TowerBridge, a closed-form recipe motivated by a first-order analysis of the hard-negative margin. Computed in seconds from 25,000 labelled pairs, it requires no model-specific tuning and leaves the architecture and inference cost unchanged. TowerBridge improves COCO test retrieval by 16.8 RSUM and Flickr30k test retrieval by 6.6 on average across all 21 evaluated CLIP checkpoints, including 8 unseen by the agent, while limiting any drop in ImageNet zero-shot accuracy to 0.5 points. It also reduces hubness on all 21 checkpoints and improves retrieval on 4 of 5 dual encoders from other families.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对 CLIP 式双编码器的 modality gap，用配对统计量定位「两塔在 hard negative 上比在匹配对上更一致」的方向，由 LLM agent 直接写出闭式权重修改而无需反传，并蒸馏为秒级可算的 TowerBridge 配方，在多个 checkpoint 上提升检索且几乎不降零样本精度。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「用统计量找出误导性一致方向、再做权重空间闭式修正」的做法，可能可供核查是否适用于抑制 VLM 内部状态中与视觉证据无关的相似性方向，或作为免训练诊断—干预模板；但论文面向检索表示而非 latent 推理，联系仍属间接。
